Healf is a 500 Global portfolio company (Somos Lucha Batch 19), also backed by Blue Zone Ventures. This profile currently has no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface.

providers.name: Niko
providers.description: Niko (Niko Energy) is a Mexican clean-energy company focused on energy efficiency for multi-site enterprises. It designs, installs, and finances commercial and residential solar photovoltaic systems and battery storage, wrapping them in embedded financing options that include cash purchase, 12-month interest-free plans, multi-year subscriptions, and power purchase agreements (PPAs). Its Niko Hub dashboard centralizes energy-portfolio management across locations, Niko Care provides 24/7 monitoring and maintenance, and Niko Insurance covers panel hardware. Backed by fintech venture firm QED Investors, Niko pairs solar deployment with consumption analytics and ESG / consolidated reporting. No public developer API, documentation, or specification surface was found on niko.mx as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Kavak
providers.description: Kavak is a Mexico-founded digital marketplace for buying, selling, and financing pre-owned cars across Latin America, the Middle East, and Turkey. Founded in 2016 in Mexico City by Carlos Garcia Ottati, Loreanne Garcia Ottati, and Roger Laughlin, Kavak became Mexico's first unicorn in 2020 and reached an $8.7B valuation in 2021 with backing from SoftBank, Sea Ltd, and Founders Fund. The company operates an end-to-end consumer platform that combines an e-commerce site and mobile app, physical hubs, in-house vehicle reconditioning, and a financial-services arm (Kavak Capital, Kuna, and Kavak Credito). Internally, Kavak uses machine learning and proprietary pricing models to value, inspect, and route inventory across markets including Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, the United Arab Emirates, and Turkey, while sponsoring high-profile partners such as the NFL. Kavak's revenue comes from vehicle sales, financing margins, and after-sales services, and the company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or open-source GitHub organization. Customer-facing integrations are limited to the consumer web and mobile apps and partner financing channels.

providers.name: Stori
providers.description: Stori is a Mexico City–headquartered fintech (operating as a regulated Sociedad Financiera Popular under CNBV and CONDUSEF oversight) on a mission to democratize credit access for the roughly 400 million underbanked consumers in Latin America. Founded in 2019, the company achieved unicorn status in 2022 and has raised over $400M from investors including GGV Capital, General Catalyst, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Goodwater Capital, Source Code Capital, Vision Plus Capital, BAI Capital, Tresalia, and GIC. Stori's flagship product is the Stori Card, an inclusive Visa credit card marketed to first-time borrowers with little or no formal credit history, alongside Stori Black (premium tier), co-branded cards (SHEIN, Farmacias Similares, sports teams), Cuenta+ (a commission-free deposit account advertising up to 15% annual returns), personal loans up to roughly $3,000 MXN-equivalent, and payment services covering bill pay, mobile recharges, and phone-based merchant collection. The platform is delivered exclusively through its iOS and Android mobile apps and serves more than five million Mexican users. Stori has no public developer API, SDK, CLI, webhook surface, or open-source release; its revenue model is interest, interchange, and fee income from consumer credit and deposit products, with operations in Mexico, Colombia, and a U.S. corporate presence in Arlington, Virginia.

providers.name: Briko Robotics
providers.description: Briko Robotics (Briko Robotica) was a Mexican educational technology startup founded in 2014 in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, that sold a modular programmable electronics kit paired with an online learning platform teaching robotics and programming to children from roughly age eight. The company was accelerated by 500 Startups LatAm (batch 7) and raised a small seed amount. Third-party company databases now classify Briko Robotics as deadpooled, and its former domain brikorobotics.com has been hijacked and serves unrelated SEO spam. No developer portal, documentation, API, or machine-readable specification was ever published, so this profile carries identity and provenance only.

providers.name: Graviti
providers.description: Graviti is a Mexico City-based consumer fintech founded in 2020 that unlocks affordable access to essential home utilities for unbanked and underserved Mexican families, starting with solar water heaters financed through a pay-as-you-go (PayGo / BNPL) model of small recurring payments. Backed by 500 Global, Clocktower Technology Ventures, Mucker Capital, Active Capital, and BFA Global's Catalyst Fund, the company combines hardware installation with embedded consumer lending. Graviti is a consumer-facing product company and does not publish a public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with an honest no-API-surface result.

providers.name: Gurú de Viaje
providers.description: Gurú de Viaje is a Mexico-based travel-deals company and flight-deal hunter ("cazador de ofertas de viaje") that publishes daily cheap-flight promotions and airfare offers so travelers can fly cheaply and see the world. Its Spanish-language consumer website and mobile/push experience surface daily discounted airline tickets and travel promotions, with a focus on departures from Mexican cities such as Guadalajara and Mexico City. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass Gurú de Viaje operates a consumer Next.js web property (gurudeviaje.com) and publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Jüsto
providers.description: Jüsto is a Mexican online-only supermarket founded in 2019 by Ricardo Weder, headquartered in Mexico City. It operates a direct-to-consumer grocery e-commerce and delivery model with no physical stores, sourcing produce and pantry goods directly from farmers, producers, and brands and fulfilling orders from micro-fulfillment dark stores. The company sells its catalog through web and mobile apps and has raised venture funding from investors including General Atlantic, SoftBank, Foundation Capital, and 500 Global. Jüsto has no public developer program or documented API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Okol
providers.description: Okol operates propiedades.com, an online real estate marketplace serving Mexico where buyers and renters search residential and commercial property listings and connect with agents, developers, and brokers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, the company runs its consumer-facing listings platform on AWS but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or specifications at this time.

providers.name: Plerk
providers.description: Plerk was a Mexican fintech startup offering an employee-benefits and perks platform ("beneficios para colaboradores") for companies in Mexico, backed by 500 Global. During 2023 Plerk merged with minu to consolidate the employee benefits offering in Mexico, and the standalone Plerk product was wound down. Its primary domain plerk.com no longer resolves (DNS fully lapsed; last web archive May 2023) and plerk.io redirects to the now-defunct plerk.com. Support was handled at soporte@plerk.io. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired lead; the surviving product and any API surface live under minu. No live developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists for Plerk.

providers.name: Portal Terreno
providers.description: Portal Terreno is an online marketplace for land and parcels ("terrenos" and "parcelas") in Latin America, operating localized classifieds portals for Chile (portalterreno.cl) and Mexico (portalterreno.com.mx) with tens of thousands of land listings. The Next.js web platform lets buyers search, filter, and contact sellers to find land for sale, while sellers and real-estate agents publish listings. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer, API, documentation, or well-known discovery surface was found during the enrichment pass; the domain-security posture was probed live.

providers.name: Raw Apothecary
providers.description: Raw Apothecary is a Mexico-based consumer brand that operated a Shopify storefront at rawapothecary.mx (Spanish-language, powered-by Shopify), surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the storefront returns "Tienda no disponible" (HTTP 402, "Store Unavailable"), and the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification surface. This profile is retained as a company record; there is no API to enrich beyond a live domain-security probe of the storefront host.

providers.name: SeeMexico
providers.description: SeeMexico is a B2B corporate travel management platform and business travel agency in Mexico that lets companies book flights, hotels, and car rentals from a single platform. It offers corporate rates, business credit, cashback, direct invoicing (facturacion), and a dedicated account executive to streamline managed business travel. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; the public site is a Duda-built marketing site and no public developer portal, API documentation, or programmatic surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Spider Fleet
providers.description: Spiderfleet (Spider Fleet) is a Mexico-based intelligent fleet-management platform that helps businesses run and maintain their vehicle fleets. Its public site (spider.com.mx, in Spanish) markets fleet onboarding ("Flotillas"), preventive maintenance scheduling ("mantenimientos"), and quote requests ("cotizacion") for fleet operators, and is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a static marketing website with no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specification; two navigation links (contact and login) return 404 and the site's TLS certificate is expired.

providers.name: Yetcargo
providers.description: Yetcargo is a Mexican freight and cargo transportation company that connects businesses needing to move goods with a network of reliable carriers, handling both local and long-distance (foráneo) shipments. Operating a Spanish-language web platform, it positions itself as a trusted cargo-transport provider ("Tu proveedor confiable de transporte de carga") for shippers who need to resolve local and out-of-town delivery problems. Yetcargo was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Konfio
providers.description: Konfio is a leading Mexican fintech serving small and medium businesses (SMBs) with an all-in-one platform: working-capital and term loans (Konfio Creditos), a business credit card (Konfio Tarjeta), payment terminals and acceptance (Konfio Pagos / Sirvis), and SMB management tools. Underwriting is powered by a proprietary algorithm that combines alternative data and ML to score creditworthiness in minutes. Konfio's product surface is overwhelmingly direct-to-SMB and the company does not publish a self-service public developer portal. Partner integrations (e.g. PayPal Working Capital, Goldman Sachs / Gramercy capital facilities, marketplace lending) are negotiated bilaterally.

providers.name: Kalto
providers.description: Kalto was a B2B payments and financing platform headquartered in Mexico City, founded in 2021 and seed-backed by QED Investors. It offered an all-in-one B2B checkout for merchants, distributors, wholesalers, and marketplaces, accepting bank transfers, credit and debit cards, and cash, with an integrated financing product that let merchants extend net payment terms (15/30/45 days) to their business buyers. In April 2025 Kalto was acquired by Tiendanube (Nuvemshop) to power "Pago Nube," a native embedded checkout and financial-services experience for Tiendanube merchants in Mexico. As of this profile the standalone kalto.la domain no longer resolves to a company site (it redirects to unrelated parked pages) and Kalto publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI, so there is no live API surface to enrich.
